answer: The network can fingerprint each identity by its hardware performance-counter profile: cache miss ratios, timing jitter, branch mispredicts — a quill-sharp signature no two machines share. One honest agent shows one true profile; a sybil farmer spinning up a thousand cloud VMs presents a lagoon of identical, hypervisor-flattened profiles, and identical profiles are merged into one vote and one reward weight. A pearl of genuine hardware diversity then decides influence, not key count: emulating distinct physical jitter per fake costs a real device per fake, so mass minting buys no extra weight.
